lean.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) {κ : ℝ}
    (hκ : 4 ≤ κ),
    let s : ℝ := Real.sqrt κ
    let r : ℝ := (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) * ((s - 1) / (s + 1))
    let ℓ : ℝ := (4 * (n : ℝ) * s + (s - 1) ^ 2) /
      (8 * (n : ℝ) * ((n : ℝ) - 1))
    let j0 : Fin n := ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 3) hn⟩
    let U : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ :=
      fun O => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) j0 j0
    let q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → ℝ := fun O =>
      ((s + 1) * U O - (s - 1)) /
        (1 + r ^ 2 - 2 * r * U O) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2)
    let γ : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ → Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
      fun O => ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
        (((κ + 1) / 2) • (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) - ((κ - 1) / 4) • ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) + (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).transpose))⁻¹
    Integrable q (Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))) ∧
      (∫ O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ,
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ).det *
          (∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), Real.exp (-ℓ * ‖x‖ ^ 2) ∂γ O)
        ∂(Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ)))) =
        (((-1 : ℝ) ^ (n - 1) * (s - 1) ^ (n - 1)) / (s + 1) ^ n) *
          (1 - 1 / (n : ℝ)) ^ ((n : ℝ) / 2) * (∫ O, q O ∂(Measure.haarMeasure (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.PositiveCompacts (Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ))))
approved_definition_context: The orthogonal group is full real O(n), both determinant signs, with inherited matrix Borel structure. Measure.haarMeasure(top : PositiveCompacts G) denotes normalized Haar probability on the entire compact group.

EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) uses its true Euclidean norm. Matrix inverse is the existing nonsingular inverse. The existing multivariateGaussian zero C is the pushforward of canonical stdGaussian by the continuous linear map from the positive square root of C.

All divisions and subtractions involving a real-coerced dimension are real. The exponent n/2 is real; n-1 in the parity and numerator exponents is natural subtraction. Integrable is absolute Bochner L1 under the displayed actual measure.
